title: add-vpc-control-plane-terraform-multi-az-peering-route53-sgs-dns
author: Priya Rao
description:
Motivation: Add a production-ready Terraform module and environment configs to provision the VPC-based private control plane across multiple AZs, with support for cross-account VPC peering, Route53 private hosted zones, interface VPC endpoints for SSM/EC2/ECR, and a hardened set of security groups. This change formalizes the recommended topology for Private deployments and codifies DNS/peering/security controls used in recent customer pilots.

What this PR contains: consolidated multi-az Terraform module (modules/vpc-control-plane) that creates: subnets (public/isolated/private) across 3 AZs, interface endpoints for SSM/KMS/ECR/ECR_DOCKER/SSM_MESSAGES, VPC peering connection resource with optional cross-account peering configuration, Route53 private hosted zone with conditional delegation records, security group templates (control plane LB, worker nodes, management-plane), and example environment configs under examples/production-multi-az/. It also includes automated tests (tflint, fmt, terraform validate) and an upgrade/rollback note for existing customers.

Scope & Limitations: This PR focuses on control-plane networking and infra required for Redwood Private (control plane only). It does not provision instance resources for workload nodes or bootstrap the application. Cross-account peering requires an explicit shared-variable flag and documented IAM prerequisites.

Testing done: local plan runs against a sandbox account with 3 AZs, tflint and terraform validate, unit tests for the module's input validation, and a staged apply to a test account (sandbox-redwood-priv-qa) with post-checks to ensure endpoints and Route53 entries appear. CI runs include a terraform plan drift check and cloudformation-lint for any associated templates.

Rollback plan: Terraform destroy is documented but for live customers we provide an upgrade guide to remove peering and Route53 delegation before destroying infra. The module supports a 'reconcile_only' mode to apply only additive changes when migrating existing networks.

Checklist: - [x] Module implemented with variables/outputs and examples - [x] tflint/terraform validate passing in CI - [x] Security group rules reviewed and least-privilege applied - [x] Documentation added to docs/private/vpc-control-plane.md - [x] Linear ticket(s) linked (ENG-2345, ENG-2378)

Related: ENG-2345 (private deployment control plane topology), ENG-2378 (multi-AZ peering for Private). Follow-up work: automatic peering acceptor automation for cross-account flows, and a migration script for existing single-AZ customers.

fix(terraform): conditional cross-account peering IAM role and acceptance flow
chore(ci): add tflint and terraform-validate CI workflow for modules
docs: add private/vpc-control-plane.md and upgrade notes
review_comments: Ethan Kim (2026-02-12): Can we add an option to disable Route53 delegation for customers managing DNS externally? Added suggestion to variables.tf to include allow_route53_delegation boolean.
Priya Rao (2026-02-13): Responded — added allow_route53_delegation + docs note about manual delegation and required NS record updates.
Marta Lopez (2026-02-15): Security review: tightened control plane LB SG to only allow management CIDR and VPC endpoints. Please ensure ssm endpoint SGs do not expose additional ports.
Priya Rao (2026-02-16): Addressed SG tightening and added automated tests to assert no 0.0.0.0/0 egress on control-plane SG.
release_notes: Adds a multi-AZ VPC control-plane Terraform module with peering, Route53 private hosted zone support, interface endpoints, and hardened security groups. Provides example configs and upgrade notes for Private customers.
risk_assessment: Medium. Changes default topology for new Private control planes but module is opt-in and includes flags for conservative migration. Cross-account peering requires additional customer IAM setup which is documented.
related_incidents: INC-2026-01 (customer pilot had DNS resolution issues due to missing delegation; fixed by documenting delegation steps)
notes_for_ops: When rolling out to existing customers, run module with reconcile_only=true first to avoid destructive changes. If peering across accounts, coordinate peering acceptance window with customer and verify Route53 delegation records post-apply.
